Power 
 Station

Technical 
 Procedure

Equipment:Insulation 
 Resistance & Polarization Index
Introduction

This 
document outlines the equipment inspection I1, which must be performed on yearly 
bases as indicated by Y1 in the title block

This test shall be performed in accordance with IEC standard 34-1 
publication and shall be made on equipment completely mounted in usual service 
condition, in dry and clean conditions, line side, neutral side and exciter terminal connections must be disconnected 
during the test

This document is initiated & tested by eng. Abdo 
Hussein Ahmed, approved by eng. Mohamed Nassr El-din Ahmed general director, 
accepted by eng. Youssef Mahmoud Aly: general director of Esna Hydraulic PS, and certified 
by 
eng. Kamel Ragheb:
HPGC 
quality control 
general director & MPIS Coordinator
Safety Precautions
A work order must be issued
The generator fire fighting out of service
Generator brake is applied
Circuit breaker of generator is opened and rack out
Connect earth switch of generator C.B
Disconnect the stand still heating of generator
Position of rotor locking bolt on position

Work to be Carried Out

Insulation resistance measurement of 
the stator winding:
Apply the voltage of 1000 
Vdc 
between each phase and frame, with the other phases connected together and to 
earth, during the test RTDS shall 
be short circuited and grounded.

sections.text:
Polarization index 
(stator):
Polarization index is the ratio of ten-minute to one-minute insulation 
resistance reading and is given by the following formula:
10 Insulation resistance
Polarization index = -----------------------
1 Insulation resistance

The PI is a useful means 
of calculation if a generator is suitable for operation

The recommended minimum 
value of PI for alternating current generator shall not be lower than (2)

When the value of PI is 
less than (2), then warm up the machine until this minimum value is obtained.

When only the one-minute 
insulation resistance value is available, it can be compared to the calculated 
recommended minimum insulation resistance for AC generator armature and field winding 
calculated by 
the following formula:
Rm = kv + 1

Where : Rm is a Minimum Insulation 
Resistance
 kv is a 
rated machine potential in kv
